m365.label: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID

mitigations.text: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkeys) and disable legacy/basic auth across the Entra ID tenant.
Block or tightly restrict the OAuth device authorization code flow via Conditional Access — EvilTokens-style device-code phishing relies on it being open.
Enable Conditional Access policies that block sign-ins from unfamiliar locations/devices and require re-auth for high-risk Graph API scopes.
Audit OAuth app consents and Microsoft Graph API activity monthly for anomalous mailbox/SharePoint access.

hunts: Hunt for OAuth device-code sign-ins followed immediately by Graph API mailbox or SharePoint access.
Search for new MFA method registrations shortly after a sign-in from a new device or location.

google-workspace.label: Google Workspace

mitigations.text: Enforce 2-Step Verification (security keys preferred) org-wide via the Google Workspace Admin policy.
Restrict third-party OAuth app access to Workspace data via the Admin console allow-list.
Enable and review Google Workspace security alerts (suspicious login, mass download/sharing) in the Alert Center.

hunts: Review Workspace login audit logs for impossible-travel and new-device sign-ins.
Hunt for bulk Google Drive sharing or download events outside business hours.

aws.label: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

mitigations.text: Disable long-lived IAM access keys for human users — require SSO/temporary STS credentials.
Enable GuardDuty and CloudTrail org-wide with alerting on anomalous API calls from new regions or IPs.
Restrict S3 bucket policies and audit regularly for public/anonymous access.
Rotate and vault any developer-held cloud credentials; scan repos and CI for leaked AWS keys.

hunts: Hunt for AWS API activity using developer/CI credentials from unfamiliar IP ranges or regions.
Search CloudTrail for GetSessionToken/AssumeRole calls followed by unusual bulk S3 GetObject activity.

azure.label: Microsoft Azure

mitigations.text: Enable Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for all admin roles — no standing Global Admin access.
Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Defender for Identity across all subscriptions.
Review Azure AD app registrations and service principal credentials quarterly for unused or over-privileged entries.

hunts: Hunt for new Azure AD app registrations granted high-privilege Graph API scopes (Mail.Read, Directory.ReadWrite.All).
Search sign-in logs for token replay indicators — the same token used from disparate IPs or geographies.

gcp.label: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

mitigations.text: Disable service account key downloads where possible; use Workload Identity Federation instead.
Enable Security Command Center and audit IAM bindings for overly broad roles (Owner/Editor) at the project level.
Restrict and log access to GCS buckets containing sensitive data.

hunts: Hunt for service account key creation or download events outside of CI/CD pipelines.
Search Cloud Audit Logs for IAM policy changes granting broad roles to new principals.

sso-idp.label: SSO / Identity Provider (Okta, Ping, etc.)

mitigations.text: Require phishing-resistant MFA (hardware keys/passkeys) for IdP admin and helpdesk accounts specifically — these are the highest-value vishing targets.
Implement out-of-band verification for any helpdesk-initiated MFA reset or new-device enrollment request.
Enable IdP session/token binding and shorten session lifetimes for high-privilege roles.

hunts: Hunt for new MFA factor enrollments initiated via helpdesk/support tickets without independent verification.
Search IdP logs for repeated failed MFA pushes followed by a successful approval (MFA fatigue pattern).

file-sharing-collab.label: Cloud File Sharing & Collaboration (SharePoint, Slack, Teams, Dropbox)

mitigations.text: Disable external Teams/Slack access by default, or restrict it to an allow-list of verified domains — helpdesk-impersonation vishing relies on open external messaging.
Block or alert on uploads/downloads to consumer cloud storage (Dropbox, pCloud, MEGA) from corporate endpoints.
Train staff to verify any 'IT support' contact arriving via Teams/Slack chat through a second channel before acting.

hunts: Hunt for inbound Teams/Slack messages from external tenants followed by remote-access tool installation.
Search proxy/EDR logs for uploads to Zoho WorkDrive, pCloud, Yandex Disk, or similar uncommon cloud storage.

source-control-cicd.label: Source Control & CI/CD (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps)

mitigations.text: Enforce 2FA and short-lived tokens (OIDC) for all CI/CD and package-registry accounts — no long-lived npm/PyPI publish tokens.
Pin dependency versions and use lockfiles; enable supply-chain scanning on pull requests for new or changed dependencies.
Restrict GitHub Actions workflow permissions to least privilege and require approval for workflows from forks/new contributors.
Audit dependencies for unexpected postinstall/preinstall or git-hook scripts.

hunts: Hunt for new or modified .git/hooks (post-merge, pre-push) or npm preinstall/postinstall scripts across repos.
Search CI logs for credential or secret access (cloud keys, SSH keys, registry tokens) from build jobs that don't normally need them.
Review recently published package versions for newly added network calls or obfuscated code.

sonicwall.label: SonicWall

mitigations.text: Patch SonicWall firmware immediately upon vendor advisories — edge VPN appliances are a top initial-access vector for ransomware (Akira, Qilin, The Gentlemen all exploit public-facing edge devices).
Rotate all local firewall/VPN account credentials and any secrets stored in the appliance config after any patch or suspected exposure — retained config artifacts let attackers bypass MFA.
Disable management interfaces on the WAN side; restrict admin access to an internal management network or VPN.
Enable and centrally log SSL-VPN authentication events for anomaly detection.

hunts: Hunt for SonicWall SSL-VPN logins from new countries/ASNs or outside business hours.
Search for firewall admin-account logins immediately followed by configuration changes or new local accounts.

fortinet.label: Fortinet / FortiGate

mitigations.text: Patch FortiOS/FortiGate as soon as advisories are published — The Gentlemen and similar ransomware crews specifically target FortiGate VPN appliances for initial access using compromised admin accounts.
Rotate FortiGate admin credentials and any cached VPN secrets after patching; assume credentials may already be retained by an attacker.
Audit Group Policy for unexpected domain-wide changes pushed via GPMC — a known follow-on technique after edge-device compromise.
Restrict the FortiGate management plane to out-of-band networks only.

hunts: Hunt for FortiGate admin logins from unfamiliar source IPs followed by VPN user/policy changes.
Search for new or modified Group Policy Objects pushed domain-wide outside of change windows.
Hunt for Microsoft Defender tampering via PowerShell shortly after VPN authentication events.

paloalto.label: Palo Alto Networks

mitigations.text: Patch PAN-OS/GlobalProtect promptly on every advisory — internet-facing VPN/firewall management interfaces remain a top ransomware entry point.
Disable GlobalProtect portal/gateway management access from the internet; require internal/VPN-only admin access.
Enable threat-prevention logging and forward firewall logs to the SIEM for correlation with endpoint alerts.

hunts: Hunt for GlobalProtect VPN logins from new device fingerprints or geographies shortly before lateral-movement (PsExec/SMB) alerts.

cisco.label: Cisco (ASA / Meraki / Firepower)

mitigations.text: Patch Cisco ASA/Firepower/IOS promptly — nation-state actors and ransomware crews exploit known edge-device CVEs for initial access.
Enable account lockout/rate-limiting on VPN and webmail portals — large-scale password spraying against logistics/tech firm VPNs has been observed from nation-state actors.
Forward Cisco device syslogs to the SIEM and alert on configuration changes outside maintenance windows.

hunts: Hunt for high-volume authentication failures against VPN/webmail portals followed by a single success (password-spraying pattern).
Search for unexpected outbound C2-style traffic over common application-layer ports (443/53) from network devices themselves.

ubiquiti.label: Ubiquiti (UniFi)

mitigations.text: Disable the UniFi cloud-management/remote-access portal if not actively used, and ensure the controller is patched to the latest version.
Change default admin credentials and disable WAN-facing management access to UniFi controllers/gateways.
Segment guest/BYOD Wi-Fi networks from internal corporate VLANs at the UniFi gateway.

hunts: Hunt for UniFi controller admin logins from unfamiliar IPs or default-credential access attempts.

watchguard.label: WatchGuard

mitigations.text: Patch WatchGuard Firebox firmware promptly and review Branch Office VPN / Mobile VPN configurations for unused tunnels.
Restrict Firebox management access to a dedicated management VLAN; disable WAN management.
Enable WatchGuard Dimension/log forwarding to the SIEM for VPN authentication anomalies.

hunts: Hunt for Mobile VPN (SSL/IKEv2) logins from new devices or impossible-travel locations.

pfsense.label: pfSense / OPNsense

mitigations.text: Keep pfSense/OPNsense and all installed packages patched; remove unused packages that expand the attack surface.
Restrict the web GUI to a management-only interface/VLAN, never expose it directly to the WAN.
Enable OpenVPN/IPsec connection logging and forward to the SIEM.

hunts: Hunt for web GUI login attempts from WAN-side addresses (should be zero if properly segmented).

checkpoint.label: Check Point

mitigations.text: Apply Check Point hotfixes/advisories immediately, especially for Remote Access VPN-related CVEs.
Review Mobile Access/VPN blade configurations for legacy authentication methods and disable them.
Centralize SmartLog/SmartEvent logging for VPN authentication anomaly detection.

hunts: Hunt for Check Point Remote Access VPN logins outside expected user populations or geographies.

other-firewall.label: Other / Unmanaged Edge Device

mitigations.text: Inventory every internet-facing device (firewall, VPN concentrator, router) and confirm it receives regular firmware/security updates — unmanaged edge devices are a leading ransomware entry point.
Ensure remote management interfaces are not exposed to the internet on any edge device.

hunts: Hunt for authentication logs on any internet-facing appliance for anomalous source IPs or login times.

windows.label: Windows

mitigations.text: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging and Constrained Language Mode for non-admin users — PowerShell is the dominant execution vector across ransomware and APT intrusions.
Restrict and monitor use of PsExec/WMIC/SMB admin shares for lateral movement; alert on first-time use of these tools by a host.
Forward Windows Event Logs (including Security and PowerShell logs) to a central SIEM with tamper-evident storage — event-log clearing is a known evasion step.
Audit Registry Run-key and Scheduled Task persistence locations regularly via EDR.

hunts: Hunt for Windows Event Log clearing events on endpoints and domain controllers.
Search for PsExec/WMIC-based lateral movement originating from non-IT-admin accounts.
Hunt for new Registry Run key or Scheduled Task entries created outside of software deployment windows.

macos.label: macOS

mitigations.text: Enforce Gatekeeper/notarization requirements and block execution of unsigned or ad-hoc-signed binaries via MDM policy.
Deploy EDR with macOS coverage and monitor for unusual Python or shell-script execution from downloaded applications.
Restrict browser-stored credential access and encourage a password manager over browser-saved passwords.

hunts: Hunt for Python or shell scripts executed from Downloads, /tmp, or quarantine-bypassed applications.
Search for access to Chrome/Safari credential stores by non-browser processes.

linux.label: Linux

mitigations.text: Disable SSH password authentication in favor of key-based auth, and restrict SSH access to a jump host/bastion.
Monitor for installation or execution of RClone or similar exfiltration tools on Linux servers.
Audit cron jobs and systemd timers regularly for unauthorized persistence.

hunts: Hunt for SSH lateral movement between Linux/ESXi hosts using shared or default credentials.
Search for RClone, WinRAR, or similar staging-tool execution on Linux servers preceding large outbound transfers.

mobile.label: Mobile (iOS / Android)

mitigations.text: Enforce MDM enrollment for any mobile device accessing corporate email/data, with conditional access requiring a managed-device check.
Train users on QR-code ('quishing') phishing — malicious QR codes in emails or documents redirect mobile devices to credential-harvesting pages, bypassing email link scanning.
Restrict corporate app installs to managed app catalogs (MAM).

hunts: Hunt for mobile-device sign-ins to corporate accounts immediately following a QR-code-containing email.

chromeos.label: ChromeOS

mitigations.text: Restrict Chrome extension installs to an admin-managed allow-list via the Google Admin console — malicious/credential-stealing extensions are a growing vector.
Enable Chrome Enterprise security policies (Safe Browsing, download protection) at the organizational-unit level.

hunts: Audit installed Chrome extensions fleet-wide for newly published or low-reputation extensions with broad permissions.

nas.label: Network-Attached Storage (Synology / QNAP)

mitigations.text: Patch Synology/QNAP DSM/QTS promptly and disable internet-exposed admin/management ports — NAS devices are frequently targeted directly by ransomware and as backup-destruction targets.
Keep at least one backup copy offline/immutable and isolated from the production domain — ransomware crews prioritize destroying connected backup infrastructure.
Enable 2FA on NAS admin accounts and disable default admin accounts.

hunts: Hunt for mass file modification/encryption events on NAS shares.
Alert on NAS admin logins or snapshot/backup-job deletions from unfamiliar source IPs.

esxi.label: VMware ESXi / vSphere

mitigations.text: Place ESXi management interfaces on an isolated management network — never expose the vSphere/ESXi management plane to general endpoint VLANs or the internet.
Enable ESXi lockdown mode and require vCenter-mediated access only; disable SSH on hosts by default.
Maintain offline/immutable backups of VM datastores — hypervisor-level encryption can paralyze an entire virtualized environment in a single operation.

hunts: Hunt for SSH enablement on ESXi hosts or direct datastore browser access from endpoint subnets.
Search for mass .vmdk/datastore file modification events indicating hypervisor-level encryption in progress.

hyperv.label: Microsoft Hyper-V

mitigations.text: Isolate Hyper-V host management (and Failover Cluster Manager) on a dedicated management VLAN, separate from general AD administration.
Maintain offline/immutable backups of VM checkpoints and configuration — hypervisor encryption can affect all guest VMs simultaneously.

hunts: Hunt for bulk VM export/checkpoint deletion or mass .vhdx modification events on Hyper-V hosts.

onprem-ad.label: On-Premises Active Directory

mitigations.text: Disable NTLMv1/LM and restrict NTLMv2 where possible; monitor for forced-authentication/relay attempts (e.g. via crafted Outlook reminders or file paths).
Audit Group Policy Objects for unauthorized domain-wide changes and restrict GPO-edit rights to a small admin group with PIM/JIT access.
Implement a tiered admin model (Tier 0/1/2) so domain-controller-level credentials are never used on standard workstations.
Enable account lockout policies and monitor for password-spraying patterns against domain accounts.

hunts: Hunt for newly created or modified GPOs deployed domain-wide outside change windows.
Search for NTLM authentication to unexpected hosts (forced-auth/relay indicators).
Hunt for anomalous account-manipulation events — new mailbox folder permissions, added group memberships.

rmm.label: RMM / Remote Access Tooling (ConnectWise, AnyDesk, TeamViewer, Atera, etc.)

mitigations.text: Maintain an allow-list of approved RMM tools and alert on/block execution of any RMM software not on that list — attackers routinely install AnyDesk/ScreenConnect/Atera for hands-on-keyboard access.
Restrict RMM tool installation to admin accounts only, and require change-ticket correlation for new RMM agent deployments.
Review RMM tool access logs regularly for sessions originating outside business hours or from unfamiliar IPs.

hunts: Hunt for installation of AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, Atera, TeamViewer, or PDQ Deploy outside of approved deployment workflows.
Search for RMM tool sessions initiated immediately following a phishing/vishing-related alert.

self-hosted-website.label: Self-Hosted Public Website / Web Application

mitigations.text: Run regular vulnerability scans/pen tests against public-facing web apps and patch CMS plugins (e.g. WordPress) promptly — compromised legitimate websites are now a primary delivery mechanism for fake-CAPTCHA (ClickFix) malware campaigns.
Deploy a WAF in front of any self-hosted website and monitor for SQL-injection attempts.
Subscribe to a website-integrity monitoring service to detect unauthorized content/script injections quickly.

hunts: Hunt for unexpected JavaScript injections or new admin users on CMS-hosted websites.
Monitor outbound web logs for visitors being redirected to known ClickFix-style fake-CAPTCHA domains.

vpn-remote-access.label: VPN Remote Access for Employees

mitigations.text: Require phishing-resistant MFA on all VPN connections — VPN credential/appliance compromise is the leading initial-access vector for ransomware groups like Akira and Qilin.
Enforce device posture checks (managed device, EDR present, patched OS) before granting VPN access.
Geofence or alert on VPN logins from countries/regions where the organization has no staff.

hunts: Hunt for VPN logins from new devices/geolocations followed shortly by internal scanning or lateral-movement activity.
Search for repeated VPN authentication failures across many accounts (password spraying).

byod.label: Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)

mitigations.text: Require enrollment in MDM/MAM with a minimum security baseline (disk encryption, screen lock, OS patch level) before personal devices can access corporate data.
Use app-level containerization (e.g. Intune App Protection) so corporate data can be wiped from personal devices without a full device wipe.
Block legacy/unmanaged-device authentication to corporate email and SaaS apps via Conditional Access.

hunts: Hunt for corporate-account sign-ins from devices that have never enrolled in MDM.
Search for credential-stealer indicators (browser credential-store access) on personally-owned endpoints with EDR coverage.

msp-third-party-access.label: MSP / Third-Party IT Manages This Environment

mitigations.text: Require your MSP to use unique, audited credentials per client (no shared/global admin credentials across their client base) — MSP compromise gives attackers one-to-many access.
Require MFA and IP allow-listing on any RMM/remote-access tooling your MSP uses to connect to your environment.
Request your MSP's incident-response plan and confirm your organization is notified within a defined SLA of any security incident on their side.

hunts: Hunt for RMM sessions from your MSP originating from unfamiliar IP ranges or at unusual hours.
Review which accounts/credentials your MSP holds and confirm none are shared across multiple client environments.

ot-ics.label: OT / ICS / Industrial Control Systems

mitigations.text: Maintain a strict network segmentation boundary (e.g. firewalled DMZ) between IT and OT/ICS networks — do not allow direct routing between corporate AD and control-system networks.
Inventory all OT/ICS assets and ensure none are directly internet-reachable; remote access should go through a jump host with MFA.
Monitor IT/OT boundary traffic for protocol anomalies (unexpected Modbus/DNP3/OPC traffic crossing into IT segments).

hunts: Hunt for any network traffic crossing the IT/OT boundary outside of an approved allow-list of protocols/hosts.
Search for remote-access tool installations on OT engineering workstations.

regulated-data.label: Handles Regulated Data (PII / PHI / Cardholder Data)

mitigations.text: Implement DLP policies on egress channels (email, cloud storage, USB) for data classified as regulated (PII/PHI/PCI) — double-extortion ransomware exfiltrates this data before encrypting it.
Encrypt regulated data at rest and restrict bulk-export/API access to it with monitoring and rate-limiting (e.g. Salesforce/SaaS record exports).
Maintain a current data-flow map identifying every system that stores or processes regulated data, to scope incident response quickly.

hunts: Hunt for large/bulk data transfers (RClone, WinRAR archives, API bulk-export calls) involving systems that hold regulated data.
Monitor for exfiltration to consumer cloud storage or VPN services used to blend outbound traffic.

no-mfa.label: No Org-Wide MFA Enforcement

mitigations.text: Enforce MFA for 100% of user accounts, prioritizing VPN, email, and any cloud admin accounts first — stolen/valid credentials are the single most common initial-access technique across tracked actors.
Eliminate shared/local admin accounts without MFA; require unique credentials per admin with MFA on every login.
Enable breached-password detection (e.g. Entra ID Password Protection) and force resets on matches.

hunts: Hunt for successful logins immediately following a password-spray pattern (many failures across accounts, one success).
Search for logins to privileged accounts with no corresponding MFA challenge in the auth logs.
